headline: Hawkish Fed rhetoric spikes rate bets, but stocks shrug it off
body: Friday's session was dominated by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote, in which he sharpened his warning that inflation running above the 2% target should be the central bank's "predominant focus." Traders responded by pricing in a September rate hike, with CME-implied odds jumping from roughly 35% to 60% and the 2-year Treasury yield rising to a one-month high near 4.34%. Equities wobbled on the initial hawkish read but recovered into the close, with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all finishing the week higher -- the S&P's first winning week in three. That combination, a sharper hawkish signal met with a shallow, recoverable equity reaction, reads as a market still willing to look through near-term rate risk rather than one bracing for a policy shock.

Underneath the index-level calm, the story is more mixed. Chipmakers were the week's weak spot, with Nvidia among the hardest hit in a broad semiconductor pullback tied to rate jitters, even as the stock heads into a closely watched earnings report this week with options pricing a 5-7% move. Retail positioning leans constructive rather than fearful -- Stocktwits readings show a bullish tilt on SPY and neutral on QQQ, bitcoin pushed above $76,000, and WallStreetBets chatter is clustering around AI-adjacent names like Marvell and Google alongside sharp mention spikes in PayPal and Palantir. The more cautionary thread running through that same chatter is concentration risk: prominent voices have flagged that the broader market's health is increasingly tied to a handful of AI-spending names, a dependency few are yet pricing as an actual downside case.
